name: Vaporwave
basis: internet-era aesthetic: violet-cyan ramp, channel shift, perspective grid, full-width type (how)

lumenary.blurb: Pink and cyan dusk, a striped sun, a perspective grid and wide-set type.

facts.bestOn: Calm scenes with a clear horizon, and sculptural subjects

why: Vaporwave looks back at the 1980s and 90s as a half-remembered dream of shopping malls and corporate computers. Its colours are sunset pinks and cyans, its horizon is a striped sun over a glowing grid, and its type is wide and spaced out. The colour split at every edge adds the feel of a worn videotape.
how: Map brightness through a ramp from deep violet through magenta to cyan and near white.
Take the red of each pixel from a few pixels to the left and the blue from a few pixels to the right.
Draw the sun as a gradient disc with horizontal bars cut out of it, thicker lower down.
Draw the floor as a perspective grid: lines from a vanishing point on the horizon, with horizontal lines bunched near the horizon.
Add scanlines, and set the caption in full-width characters by shifting each letter’s character code.
history: Vaporwave emerged around 2010 and 2011 in online music scenes, with albums such as Oneohtrix Point Never’s Chuck Person’s Eccojams and Macintosh Plus’s Floral Shoppe becoming defining records. Its visuals gather early computer interfaces, Japanese advertising, classical statues and sunset gradients into one slightly eerie nostalgia.
terms: The spot on the horizon where parallel lines seem to meet.
Wide forms of letters from East Asian text standards, used here for the spaced-out look.
Shifting colour channels sideways against each other.
paragraphs: Vaporwave takes a sunset palette to extremes. Brightness goes through a ramp from deep violet through magenta to cyan and near-white. A chromatic offset then takes the red of each pixel from a few pixels to the left and the blue from a few pixels to the right, which splits the colours at every edge like a misaligned print.

The sun is a disc with a vertical gradient, with horizontal bars cut out of it (the bars get thicker lower down). The floor is a perspective grid: lines run from a vanishing point on the horizon to equally spaced points along the bottom edge, and horizontal lines are bunched together near the horizon with a power law. The caption is converted to full-width characters, the wide letters of vaporwave, by shifting each character’s code.
